September, 2024

 Bhuvan Singh Kushwah Petiti
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh Respon
 Ia No. 128294/2024 - Exemption From Filing O.T.)

This matter was called on for hearing today.
Coram :

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6932905/
1
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R Heard Mr. Arvind Gupta, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
The State of Madhya Pradesh is represented by Mr. Abhimanyu Singh, learned counsel.
2. Notice in this case was issued on 19.06.2024 and since then the State has filed counter affidavit.

It is averred SLP (Crl.) No(s).7817/2024 therein that the petitioner is accused of financial irregularities as the Incharge of the procurement center and his actions have caused financial loss to the Government.
It is also pointed out that in the Trial, 13 witnesses have already testified but 13 more are proposed to be examined.
3. In his turn, Mr. Arvind Gupta, learned counsel submits that the petitioner has been in custody for about 4 years and 8 months since he was arrested on 14.11.2019.
It is then pointed out that for the charge under Section 409 and 420 IPC, maximum sentence that can be awarded is 7 years and 10 years respectively.
Here the petitioner has been an under-trial prisoner for practically half of the maximum awardable sentence, if convicted.
4. There is presumption of innocence of the accused in Indian Jurisprudence till proven guilty in a Court of law.
The course of Trial itself cannot be a mode of punishment for the crime.
5. Having considered the above, we deem it appropriate to grant bail.
Accordingly the petitioner (Bhuvan Singh Kushwah) be released on bail in connection with the case arising out of FIR No.50/2019.
Appropriate bail condition(s) be imposed by the learned Trial Court.
6. With the above order, the Special Leave Petition is disposed of.

Pending application(s), if any,
stand closed.

(DEEPAK JOSHI) (KAMLESH RAWAT)
